q1: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON S WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM ORDERS O, COMPANY C WHERE O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' AND O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID )
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON S WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM ORDERS O, COMPANY C WHERE O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' AND O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID )
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are semantically equivalent. Both queries retrieve the names of salespersons who have no orders associated with the company named 'RED'. Q1 uses a scalar subquery with COUNT(*) = 0 to check for the absence of such orders, while Q2 uses NOT EXISTS to achieve the same result. These two approaches are logically equivalent in this context.
